name: Kohler Power Systems remote radiator / heat-exchanger cooling design guidance

specifications.metric: Typical CAC intake-air temperature rise over ambient specified by EPA engine certification
specifications.basis: Kohler white paper 'Remote Cooling Design Factors for Standby Generators', Power Systems Topics 144, RADIATOR CIRCUIT DESIGN; print date not stated on page read, r.jina.ai retrieval 2024-06-20.
"EPA emission certifications for an engine are dependent on a specific temperature rise of the intake air over ambient temperature (typically 20°C, but it varies by engine)"
"There are a few options for remote cooling systems such as cooling towers, city or pond water cooling, and remote radiators"
"Most large generators will have two distinct cooling circuits ... the engine jacket water cooling and the charge air cooling"

"To determine how far away the radiator can be from the generator, two things must be considered: static head and dynamic head. These limits can be found on manufacturer spec sheets" – no numeric head limits printed
"POWER SYSTEMS TOPICS 144", white paper 'Remote Cooling Design Factors for Standby Generators' by Alex Hischke, Senior Project Engineer, Kohler Power Systems; 8 pages; Jina published-time 2024-06-20

notes: Product/catalogue record from a page read in the GEG plant WBS sweep. Full-parameter pass 2026-11-26: 5 new printed parameters.

gaps.what: Numeric static head, dynamic head and coolant flow limits
gaps.why: White paper explicitly says limits are on manufacturer spec sheets and prints none
gaps.next_action: Use genset-specific spec sheet for head/flow numbers
